reasons: The sensitive fields are kept out by design, but no test is visible to prove it.
The file is mostly types and simple rules.

terms.meaning: a data transfer object: a fixed shape for data sent out of the server
the list of fields a database query returns

sections.name: PublicUserDTO
sections.title: Public user shape
sections.what: The fields of a user that may leave the server: id, name, avatar and experience points.
sections.why: These are the only fields the comment considers safe to show.
sections.watch_out: Adding a field here does not stop a repo from selecting sensitive ones; the comment asks people not to.

sections.name: toPublicUser
sections.title: Convert to public user
sections.what: Turns a user record into the public shape, filling a missing avatar with null and missing XP with zero.
sections.watch_out: Defaulting XP to zero can hide a missing value as zero.

sections.name: PUBLIC_USER_SELECT, LANGUAGES, Language
sections.title: Allowed fields and languages
sections.what: Lists the fields a repo may read for a public user and the two supported languages, English and Hindi.
sections.why: The comment says never to add password or email here.
sections.watch_out: The schema import sits in the middle of the file, which is unusual and easy to miss when editing.

sections.name: preferencesInput, Preferences
sections.title: Preferences rules
sections.what: Checks preferences: up to five sports with duplicates removed, and a language from the allowed list.
sections.why: Stops invalid or repeated sports reaching storage.
sections.watch_out: The five-sport limit is enforced only here, not by the database.

summary: Defines the public user shape, the allowed languages and the rules for preferences input.
purpose: Makes sure a user leaves the server only with safe fields, and that preference values are valid.
why: The file comment says this is the only way a user leaves the server, so password hashes cannot leak.
how: Describes the public user fields, picks only those when converting a user, lists the allowed languages, and checks preferences: up to five unique sports and a language from the allowed list.
inputs: A user record, or a preferences input.
outputs: A public user shape and validated preferences.
risks: A field left out of the select list will be missing, and adding a sensitive field to the select list would expose it.
debug: If user data is missing on a page, check the select list and the conversion.
